function.mechanism: Functions as a carrier solvent for food additives and flavourings, chelates metal ions (sequestrant), stabilizes foams and emulsions in egg white products, and acts as a flavoring adjuvant. Hydrolyzed in the body to citric acid and ethanol.

adi.basis: Based on JECFA ADI of 0-20 mg/kg bw/day (1984); EFSA has not yet published a dedicated re-evaluation opinion for E 1505. Data call issued May 2016.

efsa.key_finding: Approved in the EU under Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008 as carrier solvent, emulsifier, stabilizer, and sequestrant. EFSA re-evaluation pending; no dedicated scientific opinion published as of February 2026.

fda.notes: Affirmed GRAS (1994). No limitation other than current GMP. Also listed in 21 CFR 175.300, 175.320 (polymeric coatings), and 21 CFR 181.27 (plasticizer in food packaging). SCOGS Report No. 84. FEMA GRAS Publications 3 and 25.

adi.basis: NOAEL of 2000 mg/kg bw/day (4% in diet, 2-year rat study) with 100-fold safety factor. Established 1984 (28th meeting), confirmed 1999 (53rd meeting).

concerns.summary: A 2025 computational study (network toxicology and molecular docking) identified 229 theoretical neurotoxicity targets and predicted strong interactions with MAPK3, SRC, CASP3, TNF, and BCL2 proteins. However, this is purely in-silico with no in vivo or in vitro confirmation.

no_concern_confirmed: Genotoxicity: Not genotoxic in bacterial (Ames) or mammalian test systems (CIR 2002; FSCJ 2015)
Carcinogenicity: No carcinogenicity in 2-year rat studies (CIR 2002; FSCJ 2015); not classified by IARC
Acute toxicity: Very low; oral LD50 >5000 mg/kg bw in rats
Chronic toxicity: NOAEL >= 2000 mg/kg bw/day (highest dose tested) in 2-year rat studies
Metabolism: Rapidly hydrolyzed to endogenous substances (citric acid + ethanol)
Zebrafish development: ATEC showed no effects at 0.03-300 ug/L (Yun et al. 2024)
Dermal/sensitization: Not toxic dermally; clinical human testing negative for irritation and sensitization (CIR 2002, 2023)

adi_exceedance.notes: Estimated dietary intake (Japan FSCJ) is 2.3 mg/kg bw/day, well below ADI of 20 mg/kg bw/day. NOAEL provides ~870-fold margin above estimated intake. EU use limited primarily to egg white products, so actual exposure is very low.

risk_assessment.rationale: Triethyl citrate is metabolized to endogenous substances (citric acid and ethanol), occurs naturally in plant/animal tissues, and showed no adverse effects at the highest doses tested (NOAEL >= 2000 mg/kg bw/day). Japan FSCJ (2015) concluded ADI specification was unnecessary. No genotoxicity, carcinogenicity, or reproductive toxicity. GRAS in the US, approved in the EU, and endorsed by JECFA with a generous ADI (0-20 mg/kg bw/day). No bans anywhere. The only theoretical concern is a 2025 computational neurotoxicity study with no experimental confirmation. Confidence is 0.9 rather than higher because EFSA re-evaluation is still pending and the JECFA ADI is numerical (not 'not specified').
key_factors: Metabolized to endogenous citric acid and ethanol
NOAEL >= 2000 mg/kg bw/day with no adverse effects at highest dose tested
Japan FSCJ concluded ADI not necessary to specify (2015)
No genotoxicity, no carcinogenicity, no reproductive toxicity
No IARC classification, no bans in any jurisdiction
Large safety margin: ~870-fold between estimated intake and NOAEL
